A1.justification: Despite the changed title and narrowed scope, both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching authors, model suites, multilingual datasets, and retained results. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original linguistic probing experiments, multilingual error analyses, attention comparisons, steering interventions, and pretraining-checkpoint results.

after.justification: V5 retains original multilingual probing and intervention results and reports additional activation-statistics and checkpoint-selectivity analyses.

M1.justification: V4's span mean-pooling and pair/edge representation construction disappear with the classical-pipeline branch. The retained word-level method uses the same last-subword representations, ridge regression, 64-unit ReLU MLP, and class-mean steering equation. No new probe architecture or steering algorithm is introduced.

E1.justification: V5 removes the eight English classical-pipeline tasks, including their Universal Propositions, SPR1, and SemEval relation-extraction coverage. Lexical identity and inflection probing on the same six-language Universal Dependencies corpora remain, as does the English analogy analysis.

E2.justification: Random Forest comparisons are removed from inflection probing, attention analysis, and pretraining-checkpoint experiments, including v4's dedicated Appendix I. Linear and MLP probes remain. V5's steering figures also omit the Pythia-6.9B and OLMo-2-7B-Instruct series present in v4 Figures 18–19.

E3.justification: The linear separability gap changes from MLP-minus-linear accuracy to MLP-minus-linear selectivity. Expected Layer and Center of Gravity evaluation summaries are removed. Appendix H changes steering evaluation from an MLP classifier to a linear classifier while retaining 1,000 test words and the same intervention strengths. These establish reported evaluation changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V5 adds an activation-outlier investigation using maximum magnitudes and per-dimension statistics (Appendix F.2), and extends checkpoint analysis with selectivity to examine memorization during training. It also replaces the accuracy-gap analysis with a selectivity-gap analysis. The existing tokenization, error-breakdown, attention, and PCA investigations are substantially retained.

E5.justification: V5 adds descriptive variability reporting through min-max bands across models and probe types in Figure 6 and boxplots across model-language pairs in Figure 4. These summarize heterogeneity rather than repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Pipeline and Random Forest results disappear, while activation-outlier measurements and checkpoint-selectivity results are added. Steering findings change from prominent Qwen2.5 dips near 10% depth to a highlighted DeBERTa dip near 75%, under the changed classifier readout; this is not a same-setting performance improvement. The retained PCA table and all nineteen morphological error-breakdown tables have identical numerical entries.

T1.justification: The formal gap definition changes from an accuracy difference to a selectivity difference, and the Expected Layer and Center of Gravity definitions are removed. The ridge, MLP, and steering equations remain mathematically equivalent. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V5 removes the central claim that modern models rediscover the syntax-to-semantics-to-discourse pipeline. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion instead center on lexical identity versus inflection, foreground compression and steering, and distinguish early inflection stabilization from continuing lexical evolution. The introduction also adds an explicit first-systematic-analysis novelty claim.

C2.justification: V5 interprets PCA compression through outlier activations and anisotropy, emphasizes that extra probe capacity can reduce selectivity, and adds label cardinality and frequency as alternative explanations for the lexical–inflection contrast. These substantially revise the explanatory account. The existing limitations concerning representation extraction, correlational probing, and classifier-only steering are retained and relocated.

D1.justification: V5 explicitly documents complete-sentence inputs, word-form-level control-label assignment, and shared splits between probes. Random Forest implementation and hyperparameter details are removed. The retained ridge/MLP hyperparameters, model-loading identifiers, and code-access URL remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish corresponding changes in implementation.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from extending classical-pipeline BERTology to a focused multilingual morphology study. V5 substantially expands discussion of morphological probing, modern-model representation dynamics, and activation outliers, citing works such as Acs, Lasri, Cheng, Skean, Rudman, and Sun. It also adds Niu's qualification of pipeline interpretations and removes references associated with discarded components.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, introduction, conclusion, method exposition, and analysis narrative are extensively rewritten. V5 adds a dedicated Discussion section, increasingly uses lexeme terminology, moves Limitations into the main text, removes the standalone Reproducibility Statement, and reorganizes the appendices.

P2.justification: V5 switches to a two-column layout, uses averaged main-text plots with individual curves in the appendix, merges attention accuracy/selectivity displays, and changes several axis ranges. It adds activation charts, checkpoint heatmaps, a gap boxplot, and nine layer-wise tables, while removing pipeline and Random Forest displays. These changes go well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V5 offers a clearer focus, useful outlier and checkpoint-selectivity diagnostics, and more inspectable numerical results. However, revised evidence is inconsistently integrated: Figure 29 shows probability changes around 0.1–0.15 at lambda=1, while its caption claims approximately 0.9–1.0. The newly stated exclusion of mT5 from English evaluation also conflicts with Tables 2–5. These material inconsistencies alongside the analytical and presentation gains prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
